import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** store a large binary (a file, an image) for your app and read it back.

Blobs live outside the app's state: the bytes go to the cluster's sealed blob
store, and the state keeps a `BlobRef`, the blob's SHA-256. A reference in state
is what keeps a blob: drop the reference and the blob goes. The store and its
replication are in the [blobs reference](/protocol/blobs/).

## Keep a blob a client uploaded

A client uploads to `POST /apps/{app}/blobs` and gets back the blob's id (64
hex digits). It then calls a method with that id; a `BlobRef` parameter takes it
as a string:

```rust
#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct Files {
    /// The files kept, by name: a reference in state is what retains one.
    kept: UnorderedMap<String, BlobRef>,
}

pub fn attach(&mut self, name: String, file: BlobRef) -> app::Result<()> {
    let Some(info) = file.info() else {
        app::bail!(Error::NotUploaded);
    };
    env::log(&format!("{name}: {} bytes of {}", info.size, info.mime));
    self.kept.insert(&name, &file)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`BlobRef::info()` is `None` for a blob the app does not hold.

## Write a file from a run

`calimero_sdk::files` writes and reads blobs from inside the app
(`apps/v2-fixtures/files`, the sample guest):

```rust
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use calimero_sdk::files;

pub fn save_file(&mut self, data: Vec<u8>) -> app::Result<BlobRef> {
    let mut writer = files::create()?;
    writer.write_all(&data)?;
    Ok(writer.finish()?)
}

#[app::view]
pub fn file_len(&self, id: BlobRef) -> app::Result<Option<u64>> {
    Ok(id.info().map(|info| info.size))
}
```

- `files::create()` returns a `Writer` (`std::io::Write`); `finish()` gives the
  `BlobRef`. A writer dropped unfinished leaves no file.
- `files::open(&blob)` returns a `Reader` (`std::io::Read`), but only inside an
  `#[app::compute]` run: in a call, view, timer or `init` it is refused, and
  `BlobRef::info` gives the size and hash instead.
- A file a failed call wrote is not kept: only a committed call's files are.

## Let a client download one

```rust
#[app::view]
pub fn share(&self, file: BlobRef) -> app::Result<String> {
    Ok(file.grant(3600))
}
```

`grant(ttl_seconds)` (1 to 86,400) returns a grant; a client downloads with
`GET /apps/{app}/blobs/{id}?grant=<grant>`, signed in or not.

<Aside type="tip">
  Keep the bytes in blobs and only the `BlobRef` and metadata in state: a log
  entry is capped at 1 MiB.
</Aside>
